title: The model gateway and its usage log
request: Start the AI and agent layer with one model gateway. At first the owner asked to skip the intern and not depend on it; a few minutes later he changed his mind: build phases A1 and A2 in the plan's order, the intern included, package by package.
spec: dclab_rnd/models/gateway.py with complete() and stream() taking a purpose and a tier; tiers (strong, standard, cheap) set from the environment, an unset tier falling back to standard; retries with backoff on 429 and 5xx; a model_request row per call (purpose, tier, model, tokens, latency, outcome, project; the prompt only when DCLAB_LOG_PROMPTS=1) through an Alembic migration; every caller moved onto it. Done when no openai.OpenAI( or ChatClient( exists outside the gateway, the usage table fills with a model configured, and rd-check passes with scripted clients.
plan: Find every place that creates or configures a model client: the Home agent's flow, the intern, the evidence answers, the stage notes (Responses API), the campaign critic CLI and NOOA's research clients.

Move the client from intern/llm.py into dclab_rnd/models/client.py and keep intern/llm.py as an alias; make the SDK's own retry count a parameter so the intern's behaviour does not change while the gateway does its own retries.
Write the tier and purpose settings, the usage log (a file, or the model_request table on PostgreSQL, migration 0002) and the gateway.
Move the Home flow, stage notes, project answers, evidence answers, the critic CLI and the campaign adapter onto the gateway; after the owner's correction, the intern too.
Add GET /api/models and the Admin page's model info; add the new settings to .env.example.
Run make check-all and an adversarial review in a fresh context; fix every finding with a test; commit.

decisions.decision: Purposes, not callers, pick a tier and a timeout, and each purpose says in words what it may be shown.
decisions.why: A tier is a cost and privacy choice that belongs to the kind of request; writing what each purpose may see is the basis for A1.3's data-limit test.

decisions.decision: Retry only transient failures, and a stream only before its first word reached the user.
decisions.why: Retrying a refusal wastes money; retrying a stream after text was shown would duplicate or contradict what the person already read.

decisions.decision: NOOA's research clients are not swapped but report each request to the usage log.
decisions.why: NOOA builds its own clients through litellm; wrapping them keeps the campaign working while every request is still counted.

decisions.decision: Store no key and no prompt in a usage row unless DCLAB_LOG_PROMPTS=1.
decisions.why: The usage log is read on Admin pages and in exports; prompts can carry the user's words.

decisions.decision: A failed usage write never loses an answer.
decisions.why: The answer was already paid for; logging is secondary to returning it.

change: New dclab_rnd/models/ (client.py moved from intern/llm.py, settings.py with tiers strong/standard/cheap and purposes with tier, timeout and what each may see, usage.py with a file log and the PostgreSQL model_request table, gateway.py with retries and backoff). Migration 0002. Callers moved: draft/api.py, studio/agent.py (stage notes and project answers moved from the Responses API to chat completions), engine.py, agentic/server.py, pages/evidence.py, pages/platform.py, agentic/agents.py (NOOA campaign adapter), llm_review.py (campaign critic). GET /api/models. tests/test_models_gateway.py with a guard that no module outside the gateway creates a client.

findings.defect: The legacy DCLAB_INTERN_MODEL setting silently stopped applying to the Home agent, evidence answers, synthetic data and parse patterns.
findings.scenario: DCLAB_LLM_BASE_URL points at a local Ollama and DCLAB_INTERN_MODEL=qwen2.5:7b. Before, every caller used that model. Now only the strong tier reads it, so the Home agent sends the default OpenAI model name to Ollama, gets a 404, pauses for 10 minutes and falls back to its script.
findings.cause: Only the strong tier's settings read the legacy variable.
findings.fix: DCLAB_INTERN_MODEL is the model for every tier that names none, before OPENAI_MODEL.
findings.test: A gateway settings test with only the legacy variable set.
findings.impact: Anyone running DCLab on a local Ollama with DCLAB_INTERN_MODEL set would find the Home agent, evidence answers, synthetic data and parse patterns sending the default OpenAI model name to Ollama, getting a 404, pausing for 10 minutes and falling back to scripts, with nothing saying the setting was now ignored.

findings.defect: A tier's key did not follow its endpoint: a tier could get no key, or be sent another provider's key.
findings.scenario: With only DCLAB_TIER_STANDARD_API_KEY set, the intern, evidence answers and parse patterns got no client at all. The other way round, a tier with its own BASE_URL (for example the Hugging Face router) and no key of its own was sent the OpenAI key.
findings.cause: An unset tier inherited the standard tier's URL and model but read its key from OPENAI_API_KEY.
findings.fix: A tier inherits the standard tier's key only when it has no BASE_URL of its own; a key is never sent to another host.
findings.test: Gateway settings tests for both directions.
findings.impact: A tier pointed at another provider, such as the Hugging Face router, with no key of its own would send the OpenAI key to that host; the other way round, a workspace with only the standard tier's key would have no intern, evidence answers or parse patterns at all.

findings.defect: Tests and the end-to-end flows could reach a live model through the new tier settings.
findings.scenario: server.py loads .env on import. With DCLAB_TIER_CHEAP_BASE_URL set to a local Ollama (the example in .env.example), the cheap tier's key becomes 'ollama', so parse patterns and evidence answers call the local model during rd-check. The tests blanked only OPENAI_API_KEY.
findings.cause: The test environment cleared one variable, not the new DCLAB_TIER_* family.
findings.fix: DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS=1, set by the make targets and product_e2e, makes the gateway refuse every live endpoint whatever .env holds.
findings.test: A test that a configured tier under DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS sends nothing.
findings.impact: With the cheap tier set to a local Ollama, as .env.example suggests, rd-check would call a live model from parse patterns and evidence answers; with a real tier key in .env, tests would spend money and their results would depend on a model's replies.
alternatives: Blank every DCLAB_TIER_* variable in each test's environment and in product_e2e, as the reviewer first proposed: set aside for one switch the gateway itself obeys, because a list of variables to blank misses the next setting someone adds.

findings.defect: Some model requests were never counted.
findings.scenario: agentic/live_eval.py and agentic/guide_review.py subclass NOOA's ResponsesClient and never report; the guard regex ResponsesClient\( misses 'class X(ResponsesClient):'; under python -m dclab_rnd.agentic run nothing is installed, so installed() returns a gateway with no usage log and every campaign request is dropped.
findings.cause: The guard looked for constructor calls only, and the command-line entry point never installed the workspace gateway.
findings.fix: Both subclasses record each request; the guard matches the word ResponsesClient; agentic/__main__.py installs the workspace's gateway so command-line runs log to the workspace.
findings.impact: Requests from live_eval and guide_review, and every request of a campaign started from the command line, would be missing from the usage log, so the spend shown on the pages and the caps A1.2 builds on that log would undercount.

findings.defect: The intern's usage rows had no project.
findings.scenario: Every intern request was logged with project_id None, so A1.2's per-project caps could never see intern spend.
findings.cause: The intern's client was built once, without the session's project.
findings.fix: The client is bound per session with the session's project id.
findings.test: An intern test that reads the project on its usage rows.
findings.impact: A1.2's per-project caps could never see what the intern spends, so a project could run past its budget through the intern without being refused.

findings.defect: An endpoint URL with credentials would be written into every usage row and shown on three API routes.
findings.scenario: A base URL of the form https://user:password@host/v1: urlparse(...).netloc keeps user and password, so they appear in the usage log, /api/models, /api/intern and /api/platform/limits.
findings.fix: Endpoints are shown and stored as host and port only.
findings.test: A settings test with credentials in the URL.
findings.impact: An endpoint URL with a user and password would write the password into every usage row and show it on /api/models, /api/intern and /api/platform/limits, to anyone who can open those pages or export the log.

findings.defect: Two silent behaviour changes: the campaign critic gained a 4,000-token cap, and stage notes sent max_tokens, which OpenAI's reasoning models reject in chat completions.
findings.scenario: A long JSON critique is cut at 4,000 tokens and fails to parse. A stage-notes request to a reasoning model is rejected; the helper swallows the error and the critique silently disappears.
findings.cause: Moving the callers onto one chat-completions client changed their token parameters.
findings.fix: The critic keeps no token cap; OpenAI models get max_completion_tokens.
findings.test: Scripted tests for the critic and the stage notes.
findings.impact: A long campaign critique would be cut at 4,000 tokens and fail to parse, and a stage-notes request to an OpenAI reasoning model would be rejected and swallowed, so the stage's critique would vanish without an error.

findings.defect: The failure paths had no tests.
findings.scenario: Nothing checked that an answer still comes back when the usage log raises, that a paused model is not retried, or what stream() does on a transport without streaming (it fell back to complete and never called on_text).
findings.cause: Only the happy path was tested.
findings.fix: Tests for a broken usage log, the pause, and the streaming fallback.
findings.impact: A regression in any failure path (a broken usage log losing a paid answer, a paused model being retried) would pass every test; and the streaming fallback already returned text without calling on_text, so a caller waiting on on_text got nothing.

findings.defect: Setting the SDK's retry count to 0 for the gateway would have changed the intern's behaviour.
findings.scenario: The intern relied on the SDK's single retry; the gateway now retries itself.
findings.fix: The retry count is a parameter: the intern keeps 1, the gateway passes 0 and retries with its own backoff.
findings.impact: The intern, which relied on the SDK's single retry, would have lost it, so a transient failure that used to recover would end the intern's turn with an error.

outcome: Done: every model request goes through dclab_rnd/models, the intern included; NOOA's clients report to the usage log; tests cannot reach a live model. The gate passed with 369 tests on files and on PostgreSQL and all four end-to-end flows with unchanged scores; eight review findings fixed.
lessons: When a setting is split into tiers, check what every old setting meant for every caller: a legacy variable that silently stops applying changes the model in use.
A key belongs to its endpoint; any fallback that moves a URL must move the key with it, or not at all.
A guard against live calls in tests must be one switch the gateway obeys, not a list of variables each test blanks.
risks: Splitting one model setting into tiers can silently change the model a caller uses when an old variable stops applying to it.
A key must follow its endpoint; a fallback that moves a URL without its key sends one provider's key to another host.
Any new setting can let tests reach a live model unless the gateway itself refuses live endpoints under test.
Requests made outside the gateway, by subclassed clients or command-line runs, go uncounted and break the caps built on the usage log.
Usage rows and API pages can expose credentials or prompts if endpoints and prompts are stored as given.
